Senses.Note: Dry Chan is Chan made withered by inert sitting, empty stillness, or speechless withdrawal. Recorded speakers use the label critically, while Wuzhun Shifan also mocks adopting it as a self-name; occurrences where 枯禪 is merely a proper-name epithet are excluded.

EvidenceBody: Wuzhun says Cheng adopted Dry Chan as a self-name and calls that too a nail in empty space.
Poshan criticizes merely sitting a few days of dry Chan as a limited attainment.
The author explicitly defines the criticized dry Chan as sinking into emptiness and guarding stillness.
Wanshou warns that a wavering, half-present condition must fall into dry Chan and silent illumination.
Guangshou labels wordless, speechless withdrawal small-vehicle dry Chan.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Dryness becomes a public diagnosis: sitting or silence that presents itself as Chan is tested for whether anything alive can answer from it.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The headword also occurs inside the name 枯禪自鏡; those proper-name strings do not attest the critical practice label and were excluded.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: Critical descriptions of inert sitting and Wuzhun's discussion of the self-designation concern the same dry-Chan label; a person named 枯禪 is a different thing and is excluded.
